title: Added local variable and parameter renaming
body:
Closes #11

As Laurie alluded to in the linked issue, figuring out the way to go about this was not obvious, until I looked at what code runs when you rename a variable in the GUI and found the `RenameVariableTask` class.

I'm not sure what operation I can perform that would make `checkFullCommit` to return true, but I cargo-culted the checks because the original function we're copying does them.
Either way, in my testing the rename operation worked correctly, even before I added the check/commit part.
author: ian-mad

title: Allow the Ghidra URL to be controlled via environment variable
body:
I thought I'd add this so you can easily direct the GhidraMCP at other Ghidra instance(s), or default to localhost:8080

I didn't see any other obvious things to control via environment variables or I would include them here.
author: knowaveragejoe

comments.body: LGTM but I'll modify the ghidra plugin java code to also use that environment variable before merging this

> LGTM but I'll modify the ghidra plugin java code to also use that environment variable before merging this

Wouldn't that prevent cross-"host" connection though? Ghidra can easily be run on another host, virtual or otherwise, or even just on a different interface as in the case of WSL on Windows (where Ghidra might run on Windows native, but that localhost is reachable from WSL at 172.x.x.x instead of 127.x.x.x). Other routing arrangements are thinkable, too.

Or were you thinking just the port? If I understand the plugin architecture correctly, Ghidra will try to start an instance of the plugin for each tool opened, so any but the first instance will just fail to start due to port contention. I don't see how an environment variable helps here, as that is per-process, but there is only the one java process I believe?
I will close this actually in favor of parameter passing to python. I think that will be a little more configuration friendly and future compatible.

title: Support renaming local variables
body: The current exported MCP methods allow the LLM to rename functions and data labels, but it'd be great to allow the LLM to rename local variables inside functions too.
author: cjb

comments.body: Good request. I started adding it already, but didn't include it in the initial release since it was too buggy. Ghidra handles variable names oddly and they differ between the decompilation and disassembly. I'll add the capability for renaming the decompiler variable names to the next release.

title: About the demo project:ollvm_new
body:
I am new to Ghidra and know little about it.
I am trying to follow the demo in the view:ghidra_MCP_Install.mp4.
There is a project called:ollvm_new.
Where can I get it?
author: shuhongwu

comments.body: This is actually just a project name I created myself as a sample for the demonstration. You can import any file you like into ghidra, though. To make a new project in ghidra, go to File -> New Project, and enter your desired project name. Then when you have a new project, drag and drop the binary you'd like to analyze to import it, then you can simply double click it. Good luck!
